methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Left hand, right hand: Virginia cools on data centers even as state policy promotes the AI that requires them
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's policy incoherence—promoting AI statewide while blocking the data center infrastructure AI requires—risks leaving underserved regions unable to build either the physical or educational infrastructure for deep AI capability, widening existing divides.

signals.title: Meta, Google invest in skilled worker training to build Virginia data centers - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Meta and Google investing in skilled worker training specifically to build Richmond-area data centers signals deep capability concentration in metro hubs with existing infrastructure advantages, rather than distributed workforce development across rural Virginia.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College launching a WorkAI Lab represents institutional investment in deep AI literacy outside traditional tech corridors, potentially creating peer networks that could distribute capability beyond NoVA if sustained and replicated regionally.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops in Hampton Roads signal grassroots efforts to build distributed AI fluency through peer learning networks, though success depends on whether shallow exposure deepens into sustained capability-building beyond initial training.

signals.title: Danville Field Notes: BWXT employees earn data science certifications through Danville workforce development program
signals.signal_reading: BWXT employees in Danville earning data science certifications through local workforce programs demonstrates that deep AI/data capability can emerge in historically underserved regions when anchored by existing industrial employers investing in worker upskilling.
